newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Dostum, Rabbani in significant Afghan meeting.
newsitem.headline: Dostum, Rabbani in significant Afghan meeting.

text.p: Afghan warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum and ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani met in this dusty city on Tuesday for talks that could prove ominous for the ruling Taleban Islamic militia.
Dostum, a powerful rival to the Taleban, and Rabbani embraced on a highway near here and proceeded in a convoy to a military base for talks.

The meeting followed a report from a senior Afghan diplomat that Dostum, who commands troops in northern Afghanistan, would join forces with Rabbani in resisting the advance of the fundamentalist Taleban.

Hundreds of Dostum soldiers were standing in uniform at attention with their weapons along the road into Mazar-i-Sharif, 400 km (250 miles) northwest of Kabul. Rabbani also met a group of several hundred city dignitaries and army officials standing on one side of the highway.
After the highway formalities Dostum and Rabbani climbed into a limousine for the ride to the Kala Jangy base west of the city, which is a stronghold of Dostum's Uzbek followers.
Before he met Rabbani, Dostum told reporters he would prefer not to answer any questions until Rabbani spoke.

"Let us wait until the president is here and let him speak and then i will answer your questions," Dostum said, adding: "Masood will come today or if he cannot make it today then tomorrow," a reference to Rabbani's military commander Ahmad Shah Masood who has dug in and is facing Taleban forces near the strategic Panjsher Valley.
The highway meeting between Dostum and Rabbani occurred about 10 km (six miles) east of here.
Others in the Dostum entourage told Reuters vitually every major figure opposed to Taleban in Afghanistan would be gathering here in the next few days.
Asked if Mazar-i-Sharif was becoming the new capital of "free Afghanistan," Dostum merely smiled and turned away as the president drove up.
Earlier, Masood Khalili, Afghanistan's ambassador in India, told a news conference in New Delhi that Rabbani had won the support of Dostum against the Islamic Taleban militia.
"We have received a message in the morning. He (Dostum) is also in the coalition of the government of President Rabbani," the diplomat said.
